newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Syquest, Citrix draw call interest.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Syquest, Citrix draw call interest.

text.p: Call buyers were seen in options on shares of Syquest Technology Inc, which rose in heavy turnover, and call buyers and sellers were seen in options on Citrix Systems Inc, which fell sharply in equally heavy trade, dealers said Thursday.
Syquest rose 7/8 to 3-1/8 on volume of more than 12.7 million shares.

Options traders said there was little news to account for the stock's 39 percent rally but the company said Tuesday it had begun shipping its new hard drives. It said it had a company record $26 million backlog of orders for the product.
"There's definitely been call buyers in there," one trader said of Syquest options, which trade on the Pacific Stock Exchange.
The heaviest volume was in the August 5 calls, which traded about 2,400 contracts. The option had open interest of 3,320, which included an addition of 82 contracts Wednesday. It rose 1/4 to 3/4.
The Syquest May 5 call traded about 910 contracts and the March 5 call traded 635.
On the put side, the August 5 put traded nearly 700 contracts and the May and March 5 puts each traded more than 500 contracts.
The stock has been in a long downtrend but bounced off 1-3/4 about a week ago.
Citrix Systems slumped 15-5/8 to 10-5/8 on nearly 14 million shares after the company said Wednesday its core products may face competition from industry behemoth Microsoft Corp.
On Thursday, Citrix said its relationship with Microsoft "remains strong."
Microsoft said separately it was working on integrating a multi-user capability into its Windows NT server software, now offered by Citrix.
One options trader said it appeared investors were buying and selling Citrix calls, particularly at newly listed strike prices.
The Citrix March 12-1/2 call traded 2,345 contracts and the March 15 traded about 1,425. Both were newly listed Thursday.

Among options with existing strikes, the March 22-1/2 call traded about 785 contracts. It fell 4-7/8 to 3/8 and had open interest of 14. The March 25 put, with open interest of 74 contracts, traded 75. It rallied 11-5/16 to 13-1/2.
Trading in Citrix calls was steady in the March, April, June and September series.
